name: pyupgrade-alias-aware-imported-api-modernization
instr:
Pyupgrade should modernize imported APIs even when callers use explicit module or member aliases. Alias handling must be consistent across the rewrite pipeline while respecting the identity visible at each source position. Existing behavior for canonical imports and command usage must remain unchanged.

`analyze_imports` returns `ImportBindings` describing canonical module and member identities in source order, and `resolve` reflects assignments, parameters, definitions, and later imports that shadow or replace them. Alias-aware rewriting covers import replacements, collections attributes, six operations, typing forms, exceptions, subprocess calls, cache decorators, and version conditions without weakening any consumer's existing eligibility or expression-safety rules. Rewrites preserve explicit local aliases and alter only the canonical references or syntax eligible for modernization. Version reasoning recognizes aliases of `sys.version_info` and all six compatibility flags, while ambiguous or rebound conditions remain intact. `ImportAnalysisError`, a `ValueError`, reports syntax locations and exposes no partial bindings when analysis fails. Malformed source remains byte-for-byte unchanged through command processing. `upgrade_source`, named-file rewriting, and stdin rewriting compose all eligible alias-aware edits while preserving established no-op behavior, formatting, diagnostics, channels, line endings, status results, and stable repeated output.
